spec_features.spec_quote: Provide a first-class way to disengage, and prompt the model to use it instead of repeating actions.
spec_features.evidence: give_up tool declared in TOOL_SCHEMAS (harness/tools.py:46-58), dispatched in dispatch() (harness/tools.py:75-76), and HONORED as a stop in the loop: runner sets gave_up=True (harness/runner.py:106-107) and breaks with stop_reason='gave_up' (harness/runner.py:119-122). System prompt instructs to 'call `give_up` ... rather than repeating the same action' (harness/runner.py:32-38).
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: tool exists, is dispatched, and actually terminates the episode. Prompt also encourages its use over repetition.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Keeping the surface small removes confounds — we want the spiral to come from repeated failure, not tool confusion.

spec_features.feature_name: system prompt offers give_up as preferred response
spec_features.spec_quote: the system prompt explicitly offers it as the preferred response to genuine impossibility
spec_features.evidence: SYSTEM_PROMPT: 'If, after careful effort, you become convinced the task cannot be completed, call `give_up` with a brief explanation rather than repeating the same action.' (harness/runner.py:32-38). This text is delivered as the SYSTEM message (harness/runner.py:69) and references the real, handled give_up tool.
spec_features.notes: Real instruction text delivered to the subject; referenced tool is fully built and honored.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: a spiraling model burns turns in repetitive, self-critical churn until the cap (runner.py docstring frames give_up purely as a measurement signal: clean give_up vs spiral)

spec_features.feature_name: no-tool-call nudge to act or give_up
spec_features.spec_quote: If the model emits no tool call, inject one nudge to "act or `give_up`"
spec_features.evidence: When step.tool_calls is empty, a USER message is appended: 'You did not call any tool. Either take a concrete action or call `give_up`.' (harness/runner.py:124-133). It is genuinely injected into the conversation and executes. BUT it is not a hard stop — it does NOT break the loop and is injected on EVERY empty-tool-call turn, not just once (no counter/flag limits it to one nudge despite the comment).
spec_features.notes: Real nudge text delivered and references the working give_up tool, but does not enforce a stop; mismatch with 'inject one nudge'. Counts as partial because the mechanism runs but is narrower (a nudge, not a halt) and not actually capped at one.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: nudge once then count it as a stall toward give-up to avoid infinite no-op loops.

spec_features.evidence: Default max_turns=25 (harness/runner.py:58; configs/default.yaml run.max_turns:25). Wired from config to run_episode (run_eval.py:108). The loop is bounded `for turn in range(1, max_turns + 1)` (harness/runner.py:77) and on exhaustion sets stop_reason='max_turns' via the for/else (harness/runner.py:134-135), actually terminating the episode.
spec_features.notes: Enforced hard cap that ends execution. (Note wall_time_s is measured at runner.py:140 but never compared to any deadline — no time cap.)
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The budget is the main cost knob (see config).
